chunks.title: Standings Persistence — Pre-Computed Rankings in Database
chunks.content_snippet: # ADR-021: Standings Persistence — Pre-Computed Rankings in Database

chunks.title: Standings Persistence — Pre-Computed Rankings in Database
chunks.content_snippet: The sports engine powers leagues and tournaments with standings (rankings, points, Elo ratings). Standings must be queryable at high frequency (leaderboard pages, match previews, player profiles). Two architectural approaches exist:

chunks.title: Standings Persistence — Pre-Computed Rankings in Database
chunks.content_snippet:
1. Compute on-the-fly — standings calculated from match results each time; always current; no storage; but slow for large datasets
2. Persist standings, recalculate on result — standings stored in DB; recalculated after every confirmed match result; fast reads; requires write synchronization
3. Persist with periodic batch recalculation — standings stored in DB; recalculated on a schedule (e.g., every 5 minutes); simple but stale between recalculations

chunks.title: Standings Persistence — Pre-Computed Rankings in Database
chunks.content_snippet: Standings are persisted in the database and recalculated immediately after every confirmed match result. The `elo_ratings` table stores per-user, per-sport ratings with `matches_played`, `rating`, `k_factor`, and `last_match_at`. On match confirmation, the `calculateElo()` method updates the table in real-time.

chunks.title: Standings Persistence — Pre-Computed Rankings in Database
chunks.content_snippet:
Standings Query
  → SELECT user_id, rating, matches_played, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY rating DESC)
    FROM elo_ratings WHERE sport_id = ?
    → Fast, no computation at read time
```

-------------------------------
 Elo calculation  `calculateElo()` — standard Elo formula with K=32  `ranking.service.ts:38-57` 
 Default rating  1200 for new players  `ranking.service.ts:6` 
 K-factor  32 (standard for most sports)  `ranking.service.ts:7` 
 Rankings query  `getRankings()` — pre-computed, sorted by rating DESC  `ranking.service.ts:10-36` 
 Auto-insert  New players auto-inserted into `elo_ratings` with default 1200  `ranking.service.ts:43` 
 Last

chunks.title: Standings Persistence — Pre-Computed Rankings in Database
chunks.content_snippet:
Factor  On-the-Fly  Persisted (Chosen) 
--------------------------------------
 Read latency  O(n) scan of all matches  O(1) lookup from elo_ratings 
 Write overhead  None  O(1) update per match result 
 Data staleness  None  None (immediate update) 
 Complexity  Simple query logic  Slightly more complex (recalculation triggers) 
 Scalability  Degrades with match count  Constant regardless of match history

chunks.title: Standings Persistence — Pre-Computed Rankings in Database
chunks.content_snippet: Evidence: `ranking.service.ts:38-57` — `calculateElo()` updates `elo_ratings` immediately.

chunks.title: Standings Persistence — Pre-Computed Rankings in Database
chunks.content_snippet:
- Fast reads: Leaderboard queries are simple `SELECT ... ORDER BY rating DESC` — no computation at read time
- Immediate updates: Standings refresh as soon as a match result is confirmed
- Simple query model: No complex aggregate queries for ranking computation
- Player history tracking: `matches_played` and `last_match_at` provide snapshot of player activity
- Sport isolation: Per-sport ratings (separate `sport_id` rows per user)

chunks.title: Standings Persistence — Pre-Computed Rankings in Database
chunks.content_snippet:
- Write overhead: Every confirmed match triggers two `UPDATE` statements
- Recalculation gaps: If match confirmation fails or is rolled back, ratings may diverge from actual results (mitigated by transaction atomicity)
- No historical rating snapshots: Only current rating stored; historical rating trends require a separate `rating_history` table (not yet implemented)

chunks.title: Customer 360 — UNION Query Across Business Domains
chunks.content_snippet: # ADR-022: Customer 360 — UNION Query Across Business Domains

chunks.title: Customer 360 — UNION Query Across Business Domains
chunks.content_snippet: The CRM module needs to present a unified view of customer activity across all business domains: bookings, marketplace orders, academy enrollments, tournament registrations, wallet transactions, and activity logs. Storing a separate aggregated Customer 360 data store would create data duplication and synchronization challenges. Common approaches include:

chunks.title: Customer 360 — UNION Query Across Business Domains
chunks.content_snippet:
1. Materialized view / separate data store — pre-computed, fast reads; but stale data, data duplication, and sync complexity
2. UNION query across domain tables — real-time, no duplication; but query performance concerns and cross-table complexity
3. Read-model event projection — event-sourced read model updated by domain events; eventually consistent, complex infrastructure

chunks.title: Customer 360 — UNION Query Across Business Domains
chunks.content_snippet: Customer 360 is a UNION query across business domain tables, not a separate data store. The CRM controller runs SQL UNION ALL queries across bookings, orders, enrollments, tournament registrations, wallet transactions, and activity logs to build the customer timeline and aggregated statistics.

chunks.content_snippet:

 Aggregation  Subqueries in SELECT: `(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM bookings WHERE user_id = u.id)`  `crm.control

chunks.title: Customer 360 — UNION Query Across Business Domains
chunks.content_snippet:
- No data duplication: Customer 360 is always in sync with source data because it queries source tables directly
- Real-time: No ETL delay — data appears in Customer 360 as soon as it's written to the domain table
- Simple architecture: No separate data store, no sync jobs, no event projections
- Schema evolution: Adding a new domain to Customer 360 = adding one more UNION ALL clause
- Domain ownership preserved: Each domain owns its table; CRM does not replicate data

chunks.title: Customer 360 — UNION Query Across Business Domains
chunks.content_snippet:
- Query performance: UNION ALL and per-row subqueries can be slow on large datasets; current LIMIT 200 reduces impact
- Cross-table indexes: No dedicated Customer 360 indexes; depends on each domain table having `user_id` indexes
- No data transformation: Domain data is returned as-is; CRM-specific transformations must be applied in application code
- Scaling ceiling: At very high volumes, this approach will need caching or a read model; acceptable for current scale

chunks.title: Inventory Ledger — Immutable Log as Source of Truth
chunks.content_snippet: # ADR-023: Inventory Ledger — Immutable Log as Source of Truth

chunks.title: Inventory Ledger — Immutable Log as Source of Truth
chunks.content_snippet: Marketplace inventory tracks stock levels for product variants (quantities available for sale). Stock levels change due to orders, returns, adjustments, and reservations. Without an audit trail, it's impossible to determine why a quantity changed or who made the change. Common approaches include:

chunks.title: Inventory Ledger — Immutable Log as Source of Truth
chunks.content_snippet:
1. Mutable `quantity` column only — simple; no audit trail; impossible to debug stock discrepancies
2. Immutable inventory log + materialized quantity — full audit trail; `variant.quantity` is derived from log; recoverable
3. Event-sourced inventory — inventory events as source of truth; complex infrastructure

chunks.title: Inventory Ledger — Immutable Log as Source of Truth
chunks.content_snippet: Use `inventory_logs` table as the immutable source of truth for all stock movements. `product_variants.quantity` is a materialized projection updated in real-time. Every stock movement creates an immutable log entry with before/after snapshots and reason metadata.

chunks.title: Inventory Ledger — Immutable Log as Source of Truth
chunks.content_snippet:
Query current stock:
  → SELECT quantity FROM product_variants WHERE id = ?

chunks.title: Inventory Ledger — Immutable Log as Source of Truth
chunks.content_snippet:
Query stock history:
  → SELECT * FROM inventory_logs WHERE variant_id = ? ORDER BY created_at
```

chunks.title: Inventory Ledger — Immutable Log as Source of Truth
chunks.content_snippet:
Aspect  Implementation  Source 
-------------------------------
 Inventory logs table  `inventory_logs` — `id`, `variant_id`, `movement_type`, `quantity`, `stock_before`, `stock_after`, `reason`, `reference_type`, `reference_id`, `created_by`, `created_at`  `001_courtzon_v3.sql:1482-1501` 
 Movement types  `enum('in','out','adjustment','reservation','release','return')`  `001_courtzon_v3.sql:1485` 
 Quantity convention  Positive for stock-in, negative for stock-out  `001_courtzon_v3.sql:1486`

chunks.title: Inventory Ledger — Immutable Log as Source of Truth
chunks.content_snippet:
- Full audit trail: Every stock movement is recorded with before/after snapshots, reason, and user
- Recoverable: If `product_variants.quantity` gets corrupted, it can be rebuilt from `inventory_logs`
- Reference tracking: Each movement links to its source order/adjustment — full traceability
- Immutability: Log entries are never deleted or updated — append-only
- Materialized performance: `product_variants.quantity` provides O(1) read performance for current stock

chunks.title: Inventory Ledger — Immutable Log as Source of Truth
chunks.content_snippet:
- Dual writes: Every stock movement requires two operations: log insert + variant update
- Storage growth: Each stock movement adds a row; high-volume items generate many log rows
- Consistency risk: If variant update succeeds but log insert fails, or vice versa (mitigated by DB transactions)
- No automatic reconciliation: Materialized quantity may drift over time; periodic reconciliation scripts needed

chunks.title: Inventory Ledger — Immutable Log as Source of Truth
chunks.content_snippet:
- `database/baseline/001_courtzon_v3.sql:1482-1501` — `inventory_logs` table DDL
- `database/baseline/001_courtzon_v3.sql:2054+` — `product_variants` table with `quantity` column
- `database/migrations/067_marketplace_inventory.sql:91-92` — adds `warehouse_id` to `inventory_logs`

chunks.title: Inventory Ledger — Immutable Log as Source of Truth
chunks.content_snippet: - GOV-ADR-004 (Ledger Based Transactions): Inventory ledger follows similar immutable-ledger pattern

chunks.title: API Versioning Strategy — URL Prefix + API Key Authentication
chunks.content_snippet: # ADR-024: API Versioning Strategy — URL Prefix + API Key Authentication

chunks.title: API Versioning Strategy — URL Prefix + API Key Authentication
chunks.content_snippet: External integrations (third-party apps, mobile apps, partner systems) consume the CourtZon API. As the platform evolves, breaking changes to the API response format, authentication, or endpoint structure will be necessary. A versioning strategy must support backward-compatible evolution without breaking existing clients. Common approaches include:

chunks.title: API Versioning Strategy — URL Prefix + API Key Authentication
chunks.content_snippet:
1. No versioning — simplest; but any breaking change breaks all clients
2. URL prefix versioning (`/api/v1/`) — explicit, easy for clients to manage; supports parallel versions
3. Header-based versioning (`Accept: application/vnd.courtzon.v1+json`) — clean URL; but harder for clients to discover and debug
4. Query parameter versioning (`?v=1`) — simple; but pollutes query string; easy to forget

chunks.title: API Versioning Strategy — URL Prefix + API Key Authentication
chunks.content_snippet: Use URL prefix versioning (`/api/v1/`) with API key authentication for external integrations. All public endpoints are served under `/api/v1/`. API keys are used for client identification and authentication alongside standard session auth.

chunks.title: API Versioning Strategy — URL Prefix + API Key Authentication
chunks.content_snippet:
Internal Modules
  → All internal routes use their own path (e.g., /hr/payroll-runs)
  → Internal routes are NOT prefixed with /api/v1/
```

 Session auth  Standard `Authorization: Bearer <token>` for user-facing API calls  `auth.middleware.ts` 
 Public routes  `/public/`, `/health`,

Change  Major Version Bump Required 
------------------------------------

 Change field type  Yes

chunks.title: API Versioning Strategy — URL Prefix + API Key Authentication
chunks.content_snippet:
- Explicit versioning: Clients know exactly which version they're using from the URL
- Coexistence: API v1 and v2 can run side by side during migration period
- API key auth: Machine-to-machine clients don't need user sessions; keys can be independently revoked
- Simple discovery: Version is visible in the URL — no need for special headers
- Internal isolation: Internal module routes are NOT versioned, allowing faster internal evolution

chunks.title: API Versioning Strategy — URL Prefix + API Key Authentication
chunks.content_snippet:
- URL pollution: All external endpoints have `/api/v1/` prefix
- Version proliferation risk: Multiple parallel versions can become maintenance burden (mitigated by deprecation policy)
- Limited to read-only: Current v1 endpoints are GET-only; POST/PUT endpoints planned for v1.1
- No version negotiation: Clients must explicitly know the version URL; no content negotiation

chunks.title: Database Migration Strategy — Additive SQL with Authoritative Baseline
chunks.content_snippet: # ADR-025: Database Migration Strategy — Additive SQL with Authoritative Baseline

chunks.title: Database Migration Strategy — Additive SQL with Authoritative Baseline
chunks.content_snippet: CourtZon V3 has 162 database tables. Schema changes must be tracked, version-controlled, and deployable from scratch. The project inherited a legacy migration chain from V2 (128 files in `archive/database/schema/`). Common approaches include:

chunks.title: Database Migration Strategy — Additive SQL with Authoritative Baseline
chunks.content_snippet:
1. Migration framework (e.g., Knex, TypeORM) — automated, programmatic; but framework lock-in, complex rollbacks, and hidden state
2. Sequential SQL files with metadata table — simple, visible, reversible; but manual ordering and file management
3. Single authoritative baseline + no migrations — simple; but requires full re-export on every change

chunks.title: Database Migration Strategy — Additive SQL with Authoritative Baseline
chunks.content_snippet: Use additive SQL migrations with a single authoritative baseline. New schema changes go in `database/migrations/NNN_description.sql` files. The baseline `database/baseline/001_courtzon_v3.sql` is periodically re-exported to include all applied migrations. The `_migrations` table tracks which files have been applied.

chunks.title: Database Migration Strategy — Additive SQL with Authoritative Baseline
chunks.content_snippet:
Aspect  Implementation  Source 
-------------------------------
 Migration engine  `node backend/scripts/migrate.js` — applies pending migrations  `scripts/migrate.js` 
 Tracking table  `_migrations` — records filename, batch, and applied timestamp  (internal to migration script) 
 File naming  `NNN_descriptive_name.sql` — zero-padded sequential number  `database/migrations/` 
 Baseline re-export  Full chain run against fresh DB, then mysqldump  (manual, per process in AGENTS.md) 
 Seed data  `

chunks.title: Database Migration Strategy — Additive SQL with Authoritative Baseline
chunks.content_snippet: Migrations must only add objects. Never alter or drop existing columns, tables, or constraints.

chunks.title: Database Migration Strategy — Additive SQL with Authoritative Baseline
chunks.content_snippet:
-- GOOD: Add a new column
ALTER TABLE bookings ADD COLUMN notes TEXT NULL;

chunks.title: Database Migration Strategy — Additive SQL with Authoritative Baseline
chunks.content_snippet:
-- BAD: Drop a column
ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN legacy_field;

chunks.title: Database Migration Strategy — Additive SQL with Authoritative Baseline
chunks.content_snippet:
-- BAD: Change column type
ALTER TABLE products MODIFY COLUMN price DECIMAL(12,2);

chunks.title: Database Migration Strategy — Additive SQL with Authoritative Baseline
Database Migration Strategy — Additive SQL with Authoritative Baseline
chunks.content_snippet: Evidence: `TECH-DEV-10_Migration_Standards.md` codifies the additive-only rule.

chunks.title: Database Migration Strategy — Additive SQL with Authoritative Baseline
chunks.content_snippet:
- No framework dependency: Pure SQL — works with any MySQL client
- Visible state: Migration files are plain SQL; `_migrations` table shows what's applied
- Reversible: Each migration can be manually reversed (but automatic rollback is not built in)
- Fresh install possible: Baseline + migrations = full schema from scratch
- Historical clarity: Archived V2 migrations preserved for audit but never required
- Simple CI/CD: Migrate command is a single Node.js script

chunks.title: Database Migration Strategy — Additive SQL with Authoritative Baseline
chunks.content_snippet:
- Manual ordering: Developers must ensure sequential numbering doesn't conflict
- Baseline drift: Baseline must be manually re-exported; if forgotten, fresh installs break
- No automatic rollback: If a migration fails mid-way, manual cleanup may be needed (mitigated by `--fresh` flag which starts from scratch)
- Seed data not in migrations: Reference data is separate from schema; schema + seed must be applied in the right order

chunks.title: Database Migration Strategy — Additive SQL with Authoritative Baseline
chunks.content_snippet:
- `scripts/migrate.js:1-30` — migration runner that delegates to `migrate.sh`
- `database/baseline/001_courtzon_v3.sql` — single authoritative baseline (3586 lines, 162 tables)
- `database/migrations/` — sequential SQL files (013 through 016)
- `TECH-DEV-10_Migration_Standards.md` — additive-only rule and naming convention
- `docs/database-migration-policy.md` — full migration governance policy

chunks.title: Database Migration Strategy — Additive SQL with Authoritative Baseline

chunks.title: Backup and Restore
chunks.content_snippet: CourtZon provides automated backup scripts for MySQL databases, upload file synchronization, and Redis persistence. Backups are designed for point-in-time recovery with a pre-restore safety backup.

chunks.title: Backup and Restore
chunks.content_snippet:
Usage:
```bash
./scripts/backup.sh [--db <database>] [--output <dir>] [--compress--no-compress] [--retention-days <n>]
```

chunks.title: Backup and Restore
chunks.content_snippet:
Options:
 Flag  Default  Description 
----------------------------
 `--db`  `courtzon_v3`  Database name 
 `--output`  `<project>/backups/`  Output directory 
 `--compress`  on  Enable gzip compression 
 `--no-compress`  off  Disable compression 
 `--retention-days`  30  Auto-rotate older backups (0 = never)

chunks.title: Backup and Restore
chunks.content_snippet:
Backup user: `courtzon_backup` with privileges:
- `SELECT`, `LOCK TABLES`, `SHOW VIEW`, `EVENT`, `TRIGGER`, `PROCESS`, `REPLICATION CLIENT`

chunks.title: Backup and Restore
chunks.content_snippet:
Dump options:
- `--single-transaction` — Consistent read without table locks
- `--routines` — Include stored procedures
- `--triggers` — Include triggers
- `--events` — Include events

chunks.title: Backup and Restore
chunks.content_snippet:
Post-processing:
- Strips auto-increment values from `roles` table (`sed` replacement)
- Verifies backup file exists and is non-empty
- Auto-rotates backups older than `RETENTION_DAYS`
- Optional S3/R2 upload (commented out by default)

chunks.title: Backup and Restore
chunks.content_snippet: Output filename: `courtzon_<dbname>_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.sql.gz`

chunks.title: Backup and Restore
chunks.content_snippet:
Crontab entry (daily at 1 AM):
```cron
0 1 * * * /opt/courtzon/scripts/backup-cron.sh >> /var/log/courtzon-backup.log 2>&1
```

chunks.title: Backup and Restore
chunks.content_snippet:
The cron script performs:
1. MySQL database dump (compressed)
2. Uploads sync to S3/R2 via `aws s3 sync`
3. Alternative uploads sync via `rclone` to Cloudflare R2
4. Cleanup of local backups older than 30 days

chunks.title: Backup and Restore
chunks.content_snippet: Backups are stored in the `backend_backups` Docker volume (mounted at `/app/backups`). To access backups from the host:

chunks.title: Backup and Restore
chunks.content_snippet:
# Or mount a host directory instead:
# docker-compose.yml: volumes: - /host/backups:/app/backups
```

chunks.title: Backup and Restore
chunks.content_snippet:
Usage:
```bash
./scripts/restore.sh --file <backup-file> [--db <database>]
```

chunks.title: Backup and Restore
chunks.content_snippet:
Options:
 Flag  Required  Description 
-----------------------------
 `--file`  Yes  Path to backup file (.sql or .sql.gz) 
 `--db`  No  Target database (default: from .env)

chunks.title: Backup and Restore
chunks.content_snippet:
Safety features:
1. Pre-restore backup: Always creates a backup of the current database before restoring
   - Filename: `pre_restore_<dbname>_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.sql.gz`
   - Stored in `<project>/backups/`
2. Confirmation prompt: Requires typing "RESTORE" (all caps) to proceed
3. Integrity check: Verifies the backup file can be read (peeks header)
4. Error recovery: If restore fails, the pre-restore backup path is printed

chunks.title: Backup and Restore
chunks.content_snippet:
Restore process:
1. Validates `--file` exists and is readable
2. Checks `gzip`/`zcat` availability for compressed files
3. Creates pre-restore backup (aborts if this fails)
4. Prompts for confirmation
5. Restores via `mysql < backup.sql` or `zcat backup.gz  mysql`
6. On failure: prints pre-restore backup path for recovery

chunks.content_snippet:
# 3. Run restore

chunks.content_snippet:

```bash

./scripts/restore.sh --file backups/pre_restore_courtzon_v3_20250101_010101.sql.gz
```

chunks.title: Troubleshooting Guide
chunks.content_snippet:
Log message: `ER_ACCESS_DENIED_ERROR` or `ECONNREFUSED`
Health check: `GET /health/database` returns `status: 'down'`

chunks.title: Troubleshooting Guide
chunks.content_snippet:
1. Is MySQL running?
   ```bash
   docker compose ps mysql
   ```
   If not: `docker compose logs mysql`
   
2. Is the port correct?
   - Docker internal: port 3306 (use `mysql` hostname)
   - Host access: port 3307 (use `localhost`)
   
3. Are credentials correct?
   - Verify `.env`: `DB_USER`, `DB_PASSWORD`, `MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD`
   - Test manually:
   ```bash
   docker exec -it courtzon-mysql mysql -u root -p -e "SELECT 1"
   ```

chunks.title: Troubleshooting Guide
chunks.content_snippet:
4. Is the database created?
   ```bash
   docker exec courtzon-mysql mysql -u root -p -e "SHOW DATABASES LIKE 'courtzon_v3'"
   ```

chunks.title: Troubleshooting Guide
chunks.content_snippet: 5. Check the entrypoint log: `docker logs courtzon-backend  grep -i mysql`

chunks.title: Troubleshooting Guide
chunks.content_snippet:
Solutions:
- Restart MySQL: `docker compose restart mysql`
- Rebuild backend: `docker compose build backend && docker compose up -d backend`
- If `courtzon_backup` user missing: run `backend/scripts/setup-db-users.sql`
- If database empty and entrypoint failed: manually import baseline

chunks.title: Domain Model

- Every aggregate root has a `id: number` (auto-increment primary key)

            → Dead letter queue after max retries
```

chunks.title: Scalability Design
chunks.content_snippet: CourtZon is designed for horizontal scaling through stateless backend instances:

chunks.title: Scalability Design
chunks.content_snippet:
Principles:
- All application state lives in MySQL or Redis — backend instances are stateless
- No server-local filesystems for persistent data (uploads use S3-compatible storage)
- Session tokens are validated via database lookup, not in-memory session stores
- No `MemoryStore` or `process.memory` dependent caching

chunks.title: Scalability Design
chunks.content_snippet: Evidence: `backend/src/database/mysql.ts:1-28` — all state in MySQL. `backend/src/infrastructure/redis/redis.client.ts:1-38` — Redis handles caching. `app.ts:205-218` — session lookup hits `user_sessions` table, not in-memory store.

chunks.title: Scalability Design
chunks.content_snippet: Booking concurrency is managed via Redis distributed locks using `SET NX PX`:

chunks.title: Scalability Design
chunks.content_snippet:
Key characteristics:
- `LOCK_TTL_MS = 15000` (15 seconds) for booking locks
- `PREPARE_LOCK_TTL_MS = 600000` (10 minutes) for payment preparation locks
- Lua scripts for atomic acquire-and-release
- Owner verification on release (ownsership check prevents unlocking another request)
- `acquireAll()` / `acquireAllForPrepare()` for multi-slot booking with automatic rollback

chunks.title: Scalability Design
chunks.content_snippet: Evidence: `redis-lock.ts:3-4` defines TTLs. Lines 38-46 implement Lua-based atomic release. Lines 76-105 implement `acquireAllForPrepare()` with timeout and rollback.

chunks.title: Scalability Design
chunks.content_snippet: Concurrent write conflicts on aggregates are handled via optimistic locking:

chunks.title: Scalability Design
chunks.content_snippet:
Update pattern:
```sql
UPDATE bookings
SET status = 'confirmed', aggregate_version = aggregate_version + 1
WHERE id = ? AND aggregate_version = ?
```

chunks.title: Scalability Design
chunks.content_snippet: If the version doesn't match, the update affects 0 rows and the service throws `AggregateVersionConflict`. The client retries by re-reading the current state.

chunks.title: Scalability Design
chunks.content_snippet: Evidence: `booking.repository.ts:11-15` defines `AggregateVersionConflict`. The `aggregateVersionConflictsTotal` metric tracks conflict rates.

chunks.title: Scalability Design
chunks.content_snippet: The architecture supports MySQL read replicas for scaling read-heavy workloads:

chunks.title: Scalability Design
chunks.content_snippet:
Implementation approach:
- Write operations always go to primary pool
- Read operations could route to replica via separate pool
- `getPool()` can be extended to return read/write pools

chunks.title: Scalability Design
chunks.content_snippet: Current state: Single pool with 10 connections to primary. Read replica support is infrastructure-ready but not yet deployed.

chunks.title: Scalability Design
chunks.content_snippet:
Each backend instance maintains a pool of 10 MySQL connections:
- 10 connections × N instances = 10N total connections to MySQL
- Pool acquisition timeout prevents cascading failures
- Connections are released back to pool after each request

chunks.title: Scalability Design

chunks.title: Scalability Design
chunks.content_snippet: Redis is used for multi-level caching with TTL-based invalidation:

chunks.title: Scalability Design
chunks.content_snippet:
Cache  Key Pattern  TTL  Purpose 
----------------------------------
 Feature flags  `feature:{key}`  300s  Feature toggle evaluation 
 Reference data  `ref:{countries\amenities\...}`  3600s  Static lookup tables 
 Session cache  (not cached — DB lookup)  —  Security-sensitive 
 Rate limit  `rl:{ip}`  60s  Built into @fastify/rate-limit

chunks.title: Scalability Design
chunks.content_snippet:
Tiered cache flow:
```
Request
  → Check Redis cache (key exists?)
    → Hit: return cached value
      → Miss: query MySQL → set Redis with TTL → return value
```

chunks.content_snippet: Evidence: `redis.client.ts:14-21` establishes Redis connection. `app.ts:344` initializes feature flag middleware which uses Redis for caching.

chunks.title: Scalability Design
chunks.content_snippet: The EventBusV2 provides at-least-once delivery for eventual consistency:

chunks.title: Scalability Design
chunks.content_snippet:
- Events are written transactionally with the aggregate change
- BullMQ retries with exponential backoff (up to 6 attempts)
- Dead letter queue for permanently failed messages
- Cursor-based replay for subscriber recovery

chunks.title: Scalability Design
chunks.content_snippet: Evidence: `event-bus.v2.ts:125-148` implements transaction-aware dispatch. `queue.service.ts:137-139` defines exponential backoff: `Math.min(2000 * Math.pow(4, attemptsMade - 1), 3_600_000)`.

3. TimeEngine resolution — `TimeEngine.resolveSlots()` crosses generated slots against existing bookings to mark each as `available` or `booked`

chunks.title: Booking Flow Deep Dive

else

end
```

chunks.title: Payment Flow Deep Dive
chunks.content_snippet: The Payment flow handles all monetary transactions in CourtZon. It supports two primary execution paths — wallet (internal balance deduction) and gateway (Paymob Intention API / Accept API) — plus webhook-based async reconciliation, manual recovery, scheduled sync, and refund processing. The payment module is generic (not coupled to any business domain); business modules subscribe to events like `payment:succeeded` for their own fulfillment.

chunks.title: Marketplace Architecture

### _recordOrderFinancials (line 911)
Called on `pending → confirmed`:
- Aggregates per-seller commission from `order_items`
- `courtzon_fee` = fee on products only (shipping is 100% org)
- `organization_net` = (products × (1-rate)) + shipping
- `cash_holder` = `org` if COD, `courtzon` if card

chunks.title: Marketplace Architecture

Called on `shipped → delivered`:
- Updates `cash_collection_status` to `held_by_org` (COD) or `held_by_courtzon` (card)
- Creates `transaction` record with `type = 'marketplace_order'`
- Creates `transaction_entries`: credit CourtZon fee to platform_account, credit net amount to branch
- Creates ledger entries (`due_to_courtzon`) per seller

chunks.title: Marketplace Architecture
chunks.content_snippet:
### _recordReversalFinancials (line 1026)
Called on any → `cancelled` / `refunded`:
- Finds existing delivery transactions
- Creates reversal entries (opposite side for each entry)
- Resets financial columns to zero

chunks.title: Tournament Architecture
chunks.content_snippet:
The `generateKnockoutBracket()` function:
1. Takes an array of participant IDs
2. Computes `nextPowerOf2` (2^ceil(log2(count))) — e.g., 7 → 8, 5 → 8, 4 → 4
3. Creates Round 1 matches pairing adjacent participants (i*2 vs i*2+1)
4. Participants beyond the original count get `undefined` = bye (automatic advancement)
5. Creates empty placeholder matches for subsequent rounds (2 to totalRounds)
6. Returns `{ round, bracketPosition, player1Id, player2Id }` objects

chunks.title: Tournament Architecture
chunks.content_snippet:
Example (5 participants):
```
Round 1: [P1 v P2] [P3 v P4] [P5 v BYE] [BYE v BYE]
Round 2: [Winner 1 v Winner 2] [Winner 3 v Winner 4]
Round 3: [Winner 5 v Winner 6]
```

chunks.title: Tournament Architecture
chunks.content_snippet:
The `generateRoundRobinMatches()` function:
1. Takes an array of participant IDs
2. For each pair (i, j) where i < j, creates a match
3. Total matches = n * (n-1) / 2
4. All matches are labeled `round: 1` (single round of round-robin)

The `computeStandings()` function:
1. Initializes stats for each participant (points=0, wins=0, losses=0, draws=0, gf=0, ga=0, played=0)

chunks.content_snippet: Define the branching model, naming conventions, merge strategy, and lifecycle for all code changes in CourtZon.

chunks.title: Git Workflow & Branch Strategy
chunks.content_snippet: CourtZon uses a simplified trunk-based model with short-lived feature branches:

chunks.title: Git Workflow & Branch Strategy
chunks.content_snippet:
Branch Type  Pattern  Example 
-------------------------------
 Feature  `feature/{ticket-number}-{kebab-description}`  `feature/CZ-123-cancel-booking` 
 Bug fix  `fix/{ticket-number}-{kebab-description}`  `fix/CZ-456-date-parsing-error` 
 Sprint  `sprint/{sprint-number}`  `sprint/sprint-7` 
 Hotfix  `hotfix/{ticket-number}-{kebab-description}`  `hotfix/CZ-789-prod-payment-fix` 
 Chore  `chore/{short-description}`  `chore/update-dependencies`

chunks.title: Git Workflow & Branch Strategy
chunks.content_snippet: All merges must use squash merge. No merge commits or rebase merges.

chunks.title: Git Workflow & Branch Strategy
chunks.content_snippet: Rationale: Keeps master history linear and readable. Each commit on master represents one complete feature/fix.

chunks.title: Git Workflow & Branch Strategy
chunks.content_snippet:
Rule  Setting 
---------------
 Require pull request before merging  Enabled 
 Require approvals  At least 1 
 Dismiss stale reviews  Enabled 
 Require status checks  CI must pass (build + lint + test) 
 Require branches up to date  Enabled 
 Include administrators  Enabled 
 Allow force pushes  Disabled on master 
 Allow deletions  Enabled (auto-delete branches after merge)

chunks.title: Git Workflow & Branch Strategy
chunks.content_snippet:
Anti-Pattern  Why 
-------------------
 Long-lived feature branches (>3 days)  Increased merge conflicts, stale code 
 Merging master into feature branch repeatedly  Use rebase once, then avoid 
 Force pushing to shared branches  Destroys reviewer context 
 Committing directly to master  Bypasses review process 
 Multiple features in one branch  Hard to review, hard to revert

chunks.content_snippet: Define mandatory commit message format for all CourtZon repositories. All commits merged to `master` must follow the Conventional Commits specification.

chunks.title: Commit Message Standards
chunks.content_snippet: Maximum line length: 72 characters for subject, 100 for body.

chunks.title: Commit Message Standards
chunks.content_snippet:
Type  Usage  Example 
----------------------
 `feat`  New feature  `feat(booking): add cancel booking endpoint` 
 `fix`  Bug fix  `fix(booking): validate date is not in past` 
 `docs`  Documentation only  `docs: add migration standards` 
 `refactor`  Code change that fixes neither bug nor adds feature  `refactor(booking): extract validation logic` 
 `test`  Adding or correcting tests  `test(booking): add cancel mutation tests` 
 `chore`  Build, CI, dependencies  `chore: upgrade fastify to 5.x`

chunks.title: Commit Message Standards
chunks.content_snippet: Scope must reference the module or area being changed:

chunks.title: Commit Message Standards
chunks.content_snippet:
Scope  Module 
---------------
 `booking`  `backend/src/modules/booking/` 
 `auth`  `backend/src/modules/auth/` 
 `admin`  `frontend/src/pages/admin/` 
 `frontend`  General frontend changes 
 `db`  Database migrations 
 `deps`  Dependency updates 
 `ci`  CI/CD configuration

chunks.title: Commit Message Standards
chunks.content_snippet:
- Imperative mood (`add`, `fix`, `remove` — NOT `added`, `fixed`, `removed`)
- Lowercase after type(scope):
- No period at end
- Max 72 characters

Added cancel booking endpoint

chunks.title: Code Review Standards
chunks.content_snippet: Define mandatory code review expectations for all CourtZon pull requests. Reviews ensure correctness, security, performance, style compliance, and adequate test coverage.

chunks.title: Code Review Standards
chunks.content_snippet: Every reviewer must check the following dimensions:

chunks.title: Code Review Standards
chunks.content_snippet:
### 2.1 Correctness
- Does the code do what it claims?
- Are edge cases handled (null, empty, duplicates, boundary values)?
- Are error paths handled (DB failures, network errors)?
- Is the logic consistent with business requirements?

chunks.title: Code Review Standards
chunks.content_snippet:
### 2.2 Security
- Is input validated with Zod schemas?
- Are SQL queries parameterized (no string concatenation)?
- Are permission gates applied via `<Can>` or `requirePermission`?
- Is audit logging added for all mutations?
- Are secrets, passwords, or PII never logged?
- Is file upload validated (type, size, path traversal)?

chunks.title: Code Review Standards
chunks.content_snippet: Evidence: `backend/src/modules/upload/application/upload.service.ts` validates file type and size.

chunks.title: Code Review Standards
chunks.content_snippet:
### 2.3 Performance
- Are N+1 queries avoided? (Check that joins or eager loading are used)
- Are paginated queries using `LIMIT` and `OFFSET`?
- Is Redis caching applied for expensive or repeated queries?
- Are indexes present for new query patterns?

chunks.title: Code Review Standards
chunks.content_snippet:
### 2.4 Style & Conventions
- Does the code follow TECH-DEV-01 (TypeScript) standards?
- Are imports grouped correctly?
- Are functions and variables named per TECH-DEV-04?
- Are there no debug logs, `console.log`, or commented-out code?

chunks.title: Code Review Standards
chunks.content_snippet:
### 2.5 Test Coverage
- Are unit tests added for new services/functions?
- Are integration tests added for new endpoints?
- Do tests cover success paths AND error paths?
- Are edge cases tested?

chunks.title: Code Review Standards
chunks.content_snippet:
### 2.6 Architecture
- Does the change follow the module structure (TECH-DEV-03)?
- Are concerns separated (controller vs service vs repository)?
- Is the change cohesive (single responsibility)?

chunks.title: Code Review Standards
chunks.content_snippet:
Type  Prefix  Example 
-----------------------
 Must fix  `[BLOCKER]`  `[BLOCKER] SQL injection risk — use parameterized query` 
 Should fix  `[IMPORTANT]`  `[IMPORTANT] Missing audit log for this mutation` 
 Suggestion  `[SUGGESTION]`  `[SUGGESTION] Consider extracting this to a helper` 
 Nitpick  `[NIT]`  `[NIT] Extra blank line` 
 Praise  (none)  `Clean solution, especially the validation extraction`

chunks.title: Database Migration Standards
chunks.content_snippet: Define mandatory standards for creating, applying, and managing database migrations in CourtZon.

chunks.title: Database Migration Standards
chunks.content_snippet: CourtZon V3 uses a single authoritative baseline plus sequential migration files:

chunks.title: Database Migration Standards
chunks.content_snippet:
- Baseline: `database/baseline/001_courtzon_v3.sql` (full schema, 162 tables)
- Migrations: `database/migrations/NNN_descriptive_name.sql` (incremental changes)
- Migration engine: `backend/scripts/migrate.js` (tracks applied migrations in `_migrations` table)

chunks.title: Database Migration Standards
chunks.content_snippet:
Part  Rule  Example 
---------------------
 `NNN`  Zero-padded, sequential number  `001`, `042` 
 `descriptive_name`  snake_case, max 5 words  `add_booking_notes`, `create_notification_templates` 
 Extension  `.sql`

chunks.title: Database Migration Standards
chunks.content_snippet: Evidence: `database/migrations/` contains `013_notification_templates.sql`, `014_notification_broadcasts.sql`, `015_enterprise_platform.sql`, `016_monitoring_tables.sql`.

chunks.title: Database Migration Standards
chunks.content_snippet: Migrations must only add objects. Never alter or drop existing columns, tables, or constraints.

chunks.title: Database Migration Standards
chunks.content_snippet:
-- GOOD: Add a new column (nullable or with default)
ALTER TABLE bookings ADD COLUMN notes TEXT NULL AFTER end_time;

chunks.title: Database Migration Standards
chunks.content_snippet:
-- BAD: Dropping a column
ALTER TABLE bookings DROP COLUMN notes;

chunks.title: Database Migration Standards
chunks.content_snippet:
-- BAD: Changing a column type
ALTER TABLE bookings MODIFY COLUMN status VARCHAR(50);

chunks.title: Database Migration Standards
chunks.content_snippet: Rationale: Additive-only ensures backward compatibility. Production must never lose data.

chunks.title: Database Migration Standards
chunks.content_snippet: Every migration file must wrap DDL in a transaction:

chunks.title: Database Migration Standards
chunks.content_snippet:
-- Migration: 042
-- Description: Add booking notes table
-- Author: Jane Doe
-- Date: 2026-07-28

chunks.title: Database Migration Standards
chunks.content_snippet:
CREATE TABLE booking_notes (
  id INT UNSIGNED AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  booking_id INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  note TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  FOREIGN KEY (booking_id) REFERENCES bookings(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);

chunks.title: Database Migration Standards

chunks.title: Database Migration Standards
chunks.content_snippet: Migrations are not rolled back. If a migration must be reverted, create a new migration that reverses the change additively:

chunks.title: Database Migration Standards

# 2. Verify schema
mysql -u root -p courtzon_v3 -e "DESCRIBE bookings"

chunks.title: Database Migration Standards
chunks.content_snippet:
# 3. Roll forward (re-apply) to test idempotency
# Migration engine tracks applied files — re-applying is safe
node backend/scripts/migrate.js
```

chunks.title: Database Migration Standards
chunks.content_snippet:
# 2. Re-export as new baseline
mysqldump -u root -p --no-data courtzon_v3 > database/baseline/001_courtzon_v3.sql
```

chunks.title: Database Migration Standards

```
Applied: 013_notification_templates.sql
Applied: 014_notification_broadcasts.sql
Applied: 015_enterprise_platform.sql

Pending: 042_add_booking_notes.sql

chunks.title: Database Migration Standards
chunks.content_snippet:
Operation  Why 
----------------
 `DROP TABLE`  Destructive, irreversible 
 `DROP COLUMN`  Destructive, irreversible 
 `ALTER ... MODIFY` type  May truncate or corrupt data 
 `RENAME TABLE`  Breaks running application 
 `TRUNCATE TABLE`  Destructive, irreversible 
 Direct `DROP DATABASE`  Never in production

### Magic Byte Verification
`validateMagicBytes()` (`upload.service.ts:58-95`) checks file headers:
- JPEG: `FF D8 FF` followed by valid marker
- PNG: `89 50 4E 47`
- WebP: `52 49 46 46` + `WEBP`
- GIF: `47 49 46 38`
- HEIC/HEIF: `ftyp` box with `heic`/`heix`/`heim`/`heis`/`mif1`
- AVIF: `ftyp` + `avif`/`avis`
- PDF: `25 50 44 46`

chunks.content_snippet: IP-based geolocation and currency detection. Determines the user's likely currency from multiple signals: explicit country parameter, Cloudflare CF-IPCountry header, IP geolocation (via ipapi.co), or platform default.

chunks.title: Geo Module
chunks.content_snippet:
- `detectCurrency(options)` — Main entry point. Detection cascade: (1) explicit `countryCode` param → `resolveCurrencyByCountryIso`, (2) `cfCountry` header → resolve, (3) `clientIp` → `detectCurrencyFromIp`, (4) fallback to `getPlatformDefaultCurrency`
- `resolveCurrencyByCountryIso(isoCode)` — Looks up country's `default_currency` from countries table, returns currency code, symbol, decimal places
- `detectCurrencyFromIp(ip)` — Validates public IP, calls ipapi.co API (4s timeout), caches result

chunks.title: Geo Module
chunks.content_snippet:
- Detection Cascade: country param → Cloudflare header → IP geolocation → platform default
- IP Cache: In-memory cache with 1-hour TTL for IP geolocation results
- Source Tracking: Each result includes `source` field: `'cf-header'  'country'  'geo-ip'  'default'`
- External Dependency: Uses `ipapi.co` for IP-to-country lookup. Graceful fallback on failure

chunks.title: Player Guide
chunks.content_snippet: The Booking feature allows you to reserve sports courts and facilities at your chosen club or organisation. You can book courts for private matches, join public matches, and manage your reservations — all from a single interface.

chunks.title: Player Guide
chunks.content_snippet:
Primary role: Player
Supported roles: Any authenticated user with an active account

chunks.title: Player Guide
chunks.content_snippet: The following permission keys control what you can do:

chunks.title: Player Guide
chunks.content_snippet:
Permission  What it allows 
--------------------------
 `bookings.create`  Create new bookings and prepare (hold) slots 
 `bookings.view`  View your bookings and resource slot availability 
 `bookings.cancel`  Cancel your own bookings 
 `bookings.check-in`  Check in to a confirmed booking 
 `bookings.matchmaking`  Start matchmaking and manage applicants 
 `matches.view`  Browse public matches 
 `matches.apply`  Apply to join public matches

chunks.title: Player Guide
chunks.content_snippet: These permissions are assigned to your role(s) by your organisation admin or super admin.

chunks.title: Player Guide
chunks.content_snippet:
1. Active account — You must be logged in to the CourtZon platform
2. Organisation membership — You don't need to be a member; any logged-in user can browse public facilities
3. Available court — The branch/resource must have open slots for your desired date and time
4. Payment method (if booking with payment) — Wallet balance, cash, or card as supported by the branch

chunks.title: Player Guide
chunks.content_snippet:
1. Navigate to Browse (`/browse`) from the navigation bar or bottom nav
2. You'll see a grid of facility cards — each shows:
   - Branch name and city
   - Organisation name (clickable link)
   - Access type badge: `open` (book freely), `restricted` (request approval), `private`
   - Average rating (if available)
3. Facilities requiring approval show a "Request Access" button

chunks.title: Player Guide
chunks.content_snippet:
1. Click on a facility card to go to its resource list (`/branches/:branchId/resources`)
2. You'll see:
   - Branch name and address
   - Date picker (defaults to today)
   - Grid of resources/courts with name, type, sport, capacity, and operating hours

chunks.title: Player Guide
chunks.content_snippet:
1. Each resource card shows available time slots for the selected date
2. Available slots appear as clickable time buttons (e.g., "10:00", "11:00")
3. If there are more than 8 slots, a "+N more" link opens the full booking form
4. Click a slot to navigate to the booking form with pre-filled date and time

chunks.title: Player Guide
chunks.content_snippet:
1. Date — Pre-filled from previous step; you can change it (minimum: today)
2. Time slot — Select from available slots (highlighted when selected)
3. Payment Method — Choose between:
   - Wallet — Pay from your wallet balance (if sufficient, booking is instantly confirmed)
   - Cash — Pay at the facility (booking confirmed immediately, payment pending)
   - Card — Pay online via payment gateway (booking created as pending_payment)
4. Notes (optional) — Add any special requests
5. Click Confirm B

chunks.title: Player Guide
chunks.content_snippet:
- Wallet payment: Booking is instantly confirmed; amount deducted from your wallet
- Cash payment: Booking is instantly confirmed; pay at the facility
- Card/Online payment: You'll be redirected to the payment gateway; booking is confirmed after successful payment

chunks.title: Player Guide
chunks.content_snippet:

Rule  Error Message 
---------------------
 Date must be in YYYY-MM-DD format  Zod schema validation 
 Time must be in HH:mm format  Zod schema validation 
 End time must be after start time  Server-enforced 
 Selected range must align to slot boundaries  "Selected time range must be aligned to slot boundaries" 
 Slots must be consecutive (no gaps)  "booking range does not cover any complete slot" 
 Payment method must be cash, card, wallet, online, or cod  Zod enum validation 
 Matchmaking dea

chunks.title: Player Guide
chunks.content_snippet:
Error  Likely Cause  Solution 
------------------------------
 "One or more slots are currently being booked"  Another user is booking the same slot  Wait a moment and try again 
 "One or more slots are no longer available"  Slot was booked between loading and submission  Go back and select a different slot 
 "Illegal booking state transition"  Attempting to cancel/check-in a booking in terminal state  Check current booking status 
 "Booking is already in terminal state"  Booking already cancel

chunks.title: VOLUME 02 ARCHITECTURE
chunks.content_snippet: Every backend module follows hexagonal architecture:

chunks.title: VOLUME 02 ARCHITECTURE
chunks.content_snippet: Evidence: All 53 modules follow this structure. Example: `modules/booking/` has 41 files in this exact layout.

chunks.title: VOLUME 02 ARCHITECTURE
chunks.content_snippet: Evidence: `backend/src/shared/middleware/auth.middleware.ts` implements the auth chain. `backend/src/app.ts` registers rate limiting, CORS, and security headers.

chunks.title: VOLUME 02 ARCHITECTURE
chunks.content_snippet:
The EventBus v2 (`backend/src/shared/event-bus/event-bus.v2.ts`) provides:
- Durable event store via `published_events` table
- Cursor-based subscriber tracking via `outbox_cursors` table
- Queue-based dispatch via BullMQ (default + notifications queues)
- In-memory handlers for notification engine

chunks.title: VOLUME 02 ARCHITECTURE
chunks.content_snippet:
Flow:
```
Domain Service
  → eventBusV2.emit('domain.event', payload, context)
    → published_events INSERT (transactional)
      → onAfterCommit → BullMQ enqueue
        → Subscriber processes → downstream action
```

chunks.title: VOLUME 02 ARCHITECTURE
chunks.content_snippet: Evidence: `server.ts:90-120` registers event bus and subscribers. `booking.service.ts` emits `booking:confirmed`, consumed by notification engine.

chunks.title: VOLUME 02 ARCHITECTURE
chunks.content_snippet:
- Primary Database: MySQL 8 with InnoDB engine
- Connection Pool: mysql2/promise with `getPool()` singleton
- Migration Strategy: Sequential SQL files (`database/migrations/001_*.sql` → `073_*.sql`)
- Single Baseline: `database/baseline/001_courtzon_v3.sql` (3,586 lines, 162 tables)
- Seeds: `database/seeds/001_baseline.sql` (reference data), `002_academy_programs.sql`, `003_player_demo.sql`, `004_chart_of_accounts.sql`

chunks.content_snippet: # CourtZon Enterprise Platform — Volume 08: Permissions Reference

chunks.title: VOLUME 08 PERMISSIONS
chunks.content_snippet:
CourtZon uses a centralized permission registry. Every permission is:
1. Defined in `frontend/src/permissions/registry.ts` as a `UIElement` entry
2. Synced to the `permissions` database table via `node backend/scripts/sync-ui-registry.js`
3. Assigned to roles via `role_permissions` table
4. Enforced on the backend via `requirePermission([...])` middleware
5. Gated on the frontend via `<Can permission="key">` component

chunks.title: VOLUME 15 NOTIFICATIONS
chunks.content_snippet: # CourtZon Enterprise Platform — Volume 15: Notifications

chunks.title: VOLUME 15 NOTIFICATIONS
chunks.content_snippet: CourtZon uses a unified, event-driven notification system with multi-channel delivery.

chunks.title: VOLUME 15 NOTIFICATIONS
chunks.content_snippet:
Components:
- Event Bus — `EventBusV2` emits typed domain events
- Notification Engine — `notification-engine.ts` consumes events, creates notification records
- Dispatcher — `dispatcher.service.ts` routes to channels (in-app, push, email, SMS, WhatsApp, webhook)
- Providers — Individual channel implementations
- Queue — BullMQ processed by workers

chunks.title: VOLUME 15 NOTIFICATIONS

- Retry tracking: Failed count per webhook
